title: Derived internal Hom as a module over the source algebra
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $B$ be a quasi-coherent (commutative) $\mathcal O_Y$-algebra. For an $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal F$ the sheaf $\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_Y}(B,\mathcal F)$ is a $B$-module via the action of $B$ on the first argument, giving an additive functor $\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_Y}(B,-):\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y)\to\mathrm{Mod}(B)$. Its derived extension $R\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_Y}(B,-):D(\mathcal O_Y)\to D(B)$, with $D(B)$ as in [def-pc-derived-category-qcoh-algebra], is defined as follows: for $K\in D(\mathcal O_Y)$ represented by a complex $\mathcal M^\bullet$, choose functorially a K-injective resolution $\mathcal M^\bullet\to\mathcal I^\bullet(\mathcal M^\bullet)$ in $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y)$, injective in every degree [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] (the open subsets of $Y$ form a small site), and put $R\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_Y}(B,K)=\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_Y}(B,\mathcal I^\bullet(\mathcal M^\bullet))$, the complex of $B$-modules with terms $\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_Y}(B,\mathcal I^n)$. A quasi-isomorphism $\mathcal M^\bullet\to(\mathcal M')^\bullet$ induces a quasi-isomorphism $\mathcal I^\bullet(\mathcal M^\bullet)\to\mathcal I^\bullet((\mathcal M')^\bullet)$ of K-injective complexes (two-out-of-three), hence a quasi-isomorphism of these complexes [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] (with $\mathcal L^\bullet=(\mathcal L')^\bullet=B[0]$); being a quasi-isomorphism depends only on the underlying complexes of abelian sheaves, so the assignment descends to a functor $D(\mathcal O_Y)\to D(B)$. The object $R\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_Y}(B,K)$ of $D(B)$ is called the derived internal Hom with its natural $B$-module structure; its image in $D(\mathcal O_Y)$ is the derived internal Hom $R\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_Y}(B,K)$ of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] (with $L=B[0]$, computed with the same choice of resolutions).

proof.text: The scalar action, its module axioms, functoriality and additivity are the existing explicit sectionwise construction in this module. For descent, let I and eta be the source-library canonical K-injective resolution functor and resolution map. Naturality of eta and two-out-of-three show that I(f) is a quasi-isomorphism when f is. Mathlib CochainComplex.IsKInjective.quasiIso_iff turns I(f) into a homotopy equivalence. Functor.mapHomotopyEquiv sends this equivalence through the additive algebra-valued Hom functor, and homotopyEquivalences_le_quasiIso shows the resulting map is a quasi-isomorphism of B-module complexes. DerivedCategory.isIso_Q_map_iff_quasiIso then gives sheafAlgebraHomResolution_inverts. The argument is proved generically in the private helper additive_resolution_inverts and specialized to sheafAlgebraHom.

proof.text: Localization.lift defines the derived functor, and the already proved Localization.fac comparison computes it on a representative. For sheafAlgebraHomUnderlying_eq, compare the two sectionwise O-module structures on the same Hom carrier using Module.ext' and sheafAlgebraHom_underlying_linear. The generic ofPresheaf_eq helper identifies the resulting presheaves by equality of the module structures and proof irrelevance of their semilinearity witnesses; sheaf_eq identifies the sheaves. Both functors have the same maps after forgetting to abelian presheaves: scalar restriction changes neither the carrier nor the restriction and postcomposition functions. The generic functor_eq_of_comp helper uses faithful forgetting and Functor.congr_hom to prove equality of the original functors from this equality and the object equalities. The existing derivedRHomAlgebraModule_underlying obligation remains unchanged, with its planned proof in its docstring; it is not claimed proved by this partial delivery.
